mcqs.stem: Best guess: which component of a firm's system of quality management involves deciding whether to take on a new client?

choices.explanation: Resources cover people, technology, and intellectual resources.
That component evaluates the system and fixes deficiencies.
That component concerns sharing information within the firm and externally.

choices.text: Acceptance and continuance of clients and engagements
choices.explanation: Correct. Acceptance and continuance considers client integrity and the firm's ability (competence, capacity, independence) to perform the engagement.

mcqs.explanation: Acceptance and continuance considers client integrity and the firm's ability (competence, capacity, independence) to perform the engagement.

mcqs.stem: Under SQMS No. 1, what does the firm do first in its risk assessment process?

choices.explanation: Responses are designed after risks are identified and assessed.
Inspections are part of monitoring, which comes later.
Correct. Risks are identified relative to the quality objectives.
Peer review is external monitoring, not part of the firm's risk assessment process.

mcqs.explanation: Risk assessment process: establish quality objectives → identify and assess quality risks → design and implement responses.

mcqs.stem: A firm audits 150 issuers. How often is it inspected by the PCAOB?

choices.explanation: Every three years applies to firms with 100 or fewer issuer audit clients.

choices.text: Never — it undergoes AICPA peer review instead
choices.explanation: Issuer audit practices are subject to PCAOB inspection.

choices.text: Only when a deficiency is reported
choices.explanation: Inspections are regular, not triggered.
Correct. Firms with more than 100 issuer audit clients are inspected annually.

mcqs.explanation: SOX Section 104: annual inspections for firms with more than 100 issuer audit clients; at least triennially for others.

mcqs.stem: Which of the following is **not** one of the eight components of a system of quality management under SQMS No. 1?

choices.explanation: This is a component.
This is a component.
This is a component.
Correct. Billing is not a quality management component.

mcqs.explanation: The eight components: governance and leadership, the firm's risk assessment process, relevant ethical requirements, acceptance and continuance, engagement performance, resources, information and communication, and monitoring and remediation.

mcqs.stem: A partner served as engagement partner on a client's audit through last year. When may she serve as the engagement quality reviewer on the same client?

choices.text: Immediately, if she no longer serves as engagement partner
choices.explanation: A cooling-off period is required.
Correct. SQMS No. 2 generally requires two years.
Five years is the SEC time-out for lead partner rotation.
She may serve after the cooling-off period.

mcqs.explanation: SQMS No. 2 requires a cooling-off period of two years before a former engagement partner serves as EQ reviewer on that engagement.

mcqs.stem: When must an engagement quality review be completed?

choices.explanation: The review evaluates judgments made during the engagement.

choices.text: Within 60 days after the report is released
choices.explanation: The review must be completed before the report is released.
Correct. The engagement partner cannot release the report until the EQ reviewer is done.

choices.text: At the next annual monitoring cycle
choices.explanation: Monitoring is a separate component.

mcqs.explanation: The engagement partner is not permitted to date or release the report until notified that the EQ review is complete.

mcqs.stem: Who is responsible for managing and achieving quality on an individual audit engagement under AU-C 220?

choices.explanation: The EQ reviewer evaluates significant judgments but is not responsible for the engagement.
The managing partner has system-level responsibility.
Correct. AU-C 220: the engagement partner takes overall responsibility for managing and achieving quality on the engagement.
The client does not manage the auditor's engagement quality.

mcqs.explanation: AU-C 220: the engagement partner takes overall responsibility for managing and achieving quality on the engagement.

mcqs.stem: Monitoring finds that several audits failed to test journal entries adequately. What does SQMS No. 1 require next?

choices.text: Investigate the root causes and design remedial actions
choices.explanation: Correct. Monitoring and remediation includes root-cause analysis.
Withdrawal is not an automatic response.

choices.text: Report the deficiencies to each client's audit committee
choices.explanation: Reporting to clients is not the required next step.

choices.text: Wait for the next peer review to evaluate them
choices.explanation: The firm must address deficiencies itself.

mcqs.explanation: The monitoring and remediation component requires evaluating findings, determining root causes, and designing and implementing remedial actions.

mcqs.stem: A small firm performs only compilations and reviews (no audits). Which type of peer review does it receive?

choices.explanation: System reviews are for firms that perform audits (or other engagements that require a system review).
Correct. Engagement reviews apply to firms whose highest level of service is reviews or compilations; system reviews apply to firms performing audits.
PCAOB inspections apply to firms that audit issuers.
Firms performing reviews and compilations are subject to peer review.

mcqs.explanation: Engagement reviews apply to firms whose highest level of service is reviews or compilations; system reviews apply to firms performing audits.

mcqs.stem: Which is the best example of a quality risk response under the resources component?

choices.text: Adopting a policy that leadership is accountable for quality
choices.explanation: That belongs to governance and leadership.

choices.text: Assigning staff with industry expertise to high-risk engagements
choices.explanation: Correct. Assigning competent people is a resource response.
That belongs to relevant ethical requirements.

choices.text: Evaluating the integrity of a prospective client's owners
choices.explanation: That belongs to acceptance and continuance.

mcqs.explanation: Resources cover human, technological, and intellectual resources, including assigning appropriately competent and capable engagement teams.

mcqs.stem: How often must the individual with ultimate responsibility for the system of quality management evaluate it?

choices.explanation: Correct. SQMS No.

choices.text: Every three years, when peer review occurs
choices.explanation: The internal evaluation is at least annual.

choices.text: Only when a deficiency is found
choices.explanation: The evaluation is periodic, not triggered.
That is not the requirement.

mcqs.explanation: SQMS No. 1 requires an evaluation, at least annually, of whether the system provides reasonable assurance that its quality objectives are being achieved.

mcqs.stem: The engagement partner and a senior manager disagree about whether an inventory reserve is adequate. What should happen before the report is released?

choices.text: The engagement partner's view prevails and the report is released
choices.explanation: Differences of opinion must be resolved according to the firm's policies.

choices.text: It is resolved under firm policies, possibly by consultation
choices.explanation: Correct. Engagement performance requires procedures for resolving differences of opinion, and the report may not be released until they are resolved.

choices.text: The report is released and the matter is revisited next year
choices.explanation: Differences must be resolved before release.

choices.text: The senior manager documents a dissent in the audit report
choices.explanation: The audit report does not include internal disagreements.

mcqs.explanation: Engagement performance requires procedures for resolving differences of opinion, and the report may not be released until they are resolved.

mcqs.stem: A firm's leadership rewards partners mainly for revenue growth, and several recent audits were rushed to meet deadlines. Which component of SQMS No. 1 is most directly deficient?

choices.explanation: Correct. Leadership sets the culture, and incentives that prioritize revenue over quality undermine it.
Communication is not the root issue here.
No independence breach is described.
Client acceptance is not described.

mcqs.explanation: Governance and leadership includes a culture that recognizes and reinforces the firm's commitment to quality, including in performance evaluations and compensation.

mcqs.stem: Under PCAOB QC 1000, how often must a firm evaluate its system of quality control and report the result to the PCAOB?

choices.explanation: The evaluation is annual, not tied to the inspection cycle.
Correct. The firm evaluates its QC system annually as of September 30 and reports on Form QC.

choices.text: Only after a deficiency is found
choices.explanation: The evaluation is required every year.

choices.text: Never; the PCAOB does the evaluation
choices.explanation: The firm itself must evaluate and report.

mcqs.explanation: QC 1000: risk-based QC system, annual evaluation reported on Form QC.

mcqs.stem: Under SQMS No. 1, after establishing quality objectives, a firm next:

choices.explanation: Reports aren't part of the risk assessment process.
Correct. The firm then designs responses to the assessed quality risks.
Peer review isn't the next step in SQMS 1.
EQ reviews are one possible response.

mcqs.explanation: SQMS No. 1 risk assessment process: establish quality objectives, identify and assess quality risks, design and implement responses.

mcqs.stem: Under SQMS No. 1, which engagements must have an engagement quality review?

choices.explanation: EQ reviews aren't required for every engagement.
The opinion type isn't the test.
Correct. The firm also determines other engagements in response to quality risks.
First-year status isn't the requirement.

mcqs.explanation: SQMS No. 1: EQ reviews for audits of listed entities, engagements where required by law or regulation, and others the firm determines appropriate.

mcqs.stem: A firm's monitoring finds deficiencies that are severe and pervasive across its audits. What should the individual with ultimate responsibility conclude?

choices.text: The system provides reasonable assurance with exceptions
choices.explanation: Severe and pervasive deficiencies preclude that conclusion.

choices.text: No conclusion is needed until the next peer review
choices.explanation: The annual evaluation is the firm's own responsibility.

choices.text: Only the affected engagements need correction
choices.explanation: The conclusion concerns the whole system.

choices.text: The system doesn't provide reasonable assurance
choices.explanation: Correct. Severe and pervasive deficiencies mean the system's objectives aren't met.

mcqs.explanation: SQMS No. 1 annual evaluation: conclude reasonable assurance, reasonable assurance except for deficiencies that are severe but not pervasive, or that the system doesn't provide reasonable assurance.

mcqs.stem: An engagement quality reviewer disagrees with the engagement team's conclusion on a significant estimate. Which action is appropriate under SQMS No. 2?

choices.text: Raise it; the report isn't released until resolved
choices.explanation: Correct. The engagement can't be completed until the EQ reviewer's concerns are resolved.

choices.text: Change the estimate in the client's books
choices.explanation: The reviewer doesn't make engagement decisions.

choices.text: Sign the report as engagement partner
choices.explanation: The reviewer isn't the engagement partner.

choices.text: Ignore it, because the review is advisory
choices.explanation: Unresolved matters prevent release.

mcqs.explanation: SQMS No. 2: the EQ reviewer evaluates significant judgments; the engagement partner can't date the report until notified that the review is complete.

mcqs.stem: Under SQMS No. 1, which component addresses obtaining and sharing information needed for the system of quality management?

choices.explanation: That sets the tone.
That covers doing the work.
Correct. One of the eight components.
That covers people and tools.

mcqs.explanation: Information and communication addresses obtaining, generating and communicating information to support the system.

mcqs.stem: After finding a monitoring deficiency, what must the firm do under SQMS No. 1?

choices.explanation: Root cause is required.
Not for nonissuer firms.
That isn't required.
Correct. Then design remedial actions.

mcqs.explanation: Firms investigate the root causes of identified deficiencies and evaluate their severity and pervasiveness.

mcqs.stem: A firm belongs to a network that provides audit methodology. What must the firm do under SQMS No. 1?

choices.explanation: Correct. It stays responsible for its system.
The firm remains responsible.
They may be used.
Responsibility stays with the firm.

mcqs.explanation: A firm using network requirements or services understands them and determines how they affect its system.

mcqs.stem: A prospective client's owners have a history of regulatory violations. Which component addresses this?

choices.explanation: That reviews the system.
Correct. Client integrity is considered.
That covers people and tools.
That covers sharing information.

mcqs.explanation: The acceptance and continuance component addresses the integrity and ethical values of prospective clients.

mcqs.stem: An engagement team faces a difficult, contentious accounting issue. Which response does SQMS No. 1 expect?

choices.explanation: Consultation is expected.

choices.text: Defer the issue to next year
choices.explanation: It must be resolved.
Correct. Part of engagement performance.
The firm decides.

mcqs.explanation: Engagement performance includes consultation on difficult or contentious matters and documenting the conclusions.

mcqs.stem: What approach does SQMS No. 1 require for a firm's quality system?

choices.explanation: It's risk-based.
Not sufficient.

choices.text: An approach chosen by each partner
choices.explanation: It's firm-wide.
Correct. Firms set objectives, risks and responses.

mcqs.explanation: SQMS No. 1 requires a risk-based system: quality objectives, quality risks and responses.

mcqs.stem: How often must a firm evaluate its system of quality management?

choices.explanation: Correct. Leadership evaluates it yearly.
Too infrequent.
The evaluation is annual.
The evaluation is annual.

mcqs.explanation: The individual with ultimate responsibility evaluates the system at least annually.

mcqs.stem: Which engagements require an engagement quality review under SQMS?

choices.explanation: That is not required.
Correct. Plus any required by law or regulation.
That is not the rule.
That is not the rule.

mcqs.explanation: EQ reviews are required for engagements the firm's responses designate, including those required by law or regulation.

mcqs.stem: Monitoring finds weak documentation on several engagements. What should the firm do?

choices.text: Ignore them if opinions were right
choices.explanation: They must be evaluated.
That is not required.
Correct. Deficiencies need root cause analysis.
Root causes must be addressed.

mcqs.explanation: SQMS No. 1 requires investigating root causes of deficiencies and designing remedial actions.

mcqs.stem: A former engagement partner wants to become the EQ reviewer for the same client. When is this permitted under SQMS No. 2?

choices.explanation: Objectivity would be threatened.
Two years is required.
Allowed after cooling-off.
Correct. A cooling-off period protects objectivity.

mcqs.explanation: SQMS No. 2 requires a two-year cooling-off period before a former engagement partner can serve as EQ reviewer.

mcqs.stem: The EQ reviewer disagrees with the engagement partner on a significant judgment. When can the report be released?

choices.explanation: Correct. Release waits for resolution.
The EQ review isn't complete.
That is not the rule.
The firm decides.

mcqs.explanation: The report can't be dated until the EQ review is complete and differences are resolved under firm policy.

mcqs.stem: The annual evaluation concludes the quality system doesn't provide reasonable assurance. What must the firm do?

choices.explanation: The firm must act promptly.
Correct. Deficiencies require action.
The firm must act promptly.
More is required.

mcqs.explanation: When the system doesn't provide reasonable assurance, the firm takes prompt action and communicates with personnel and others as needed.

mcqs.stem: Under SQMS No. 1, which is an example of a response in the monitoring and remediation component?

choices.text: Inspecting completed engagements and analyzing root causes
choices.explanation: Correct. Monitoring and remediation: monitoring activities, evaluating findings, root-cause analysis, and remediation.

choices.text: Establishing the firm's quality objectives each year
choices.explanation: That's the risk assessment process.

choices.text: Evaluating a prospective client's integrity before acceptance
choices.explanation: That's acceptance and continuance.

choices.text: Hiring, training, and evaluating professional staff
choices.explanation: That's resources.

mcqs.explanation: Monitoring and remediation: monitoring activities, evaluating findings, root-cause analysis, and remediation.

mcqs.stem: An engagement quality reviewer disagrees with the engagement partner about a significant judgment. When may the report be released?

choices.text: Immediately, because the engagement partner has final authority
choices.explanation: Differences must be resolved first.

choices.text: Once it is resolved under firm policy and the review is done
choices.explanation: Correct. SQMS No.

choices.text: After 60 days, regardless of the disagreement
choices.explanation: No waiting period resolves the disagreement.

choices.text: Only after the PCAOB approves the release
choices.explanation: PCAOB approval isn't required.

mcqs.explanation: SQMS No. 2 and AU-C 220: the report isn't released until the EQ review is complete and differences are resolved.

mcqs.stem: Under SQMS No. 1, who must be assigned ultimate responsibility and accountability for the firm's system of quality management?

choices.text: Each engagement partner, for his or her own engagements
choices.explanation: Engagement partners manage engagement quality, not the firm's system.

choices.text: The CEO or managing partner (or equivalent)
choices.explanation: Correct. Ultimate responsibility is assigned to the CEO, managing partner or the managing board.

choices.text: An outside peer reviewer engaged by the firm
choices.explanation: Peer reviewers are external and not accountable for the firm's system.

choices.text: The engagement quality reviewer on each audit
choices.explanation: EQ reviewers evaluate specific engagements only.

mcqs.explanation: SQMS No. 1 requires the firm to assign ultimate responsibility and accountability for the system of quality management to the CEO or managing partner (or equivalent).

mcqs.stem: Under SQMS No. 2, a former engagement partner may generally serve as engagement quality reviewer on the same engagement only after a cooling-off period of:

choices.explanation: The required period is two years.
Correct. SQMS No. 2 requires a two-year cooling-off period for the former engagement partner.
Five years is the SEC partner time-out, not the SQMS No. 2 period.

choices.text: No waiting period; objectivity is presumed
choices.explanation: A cooling-off period is required.

mcqs.explanation: SQMS No. 2: a person previously serving as engagement partner should not be appointed EQ reviewer for that engagement until two years have passed.

flashcards.back: Governance & leadership; risk assessment process; ethical requirements; acceptance & continuance; engagement performance; resources; information & communication; monitoring & remediation.
Establish quality objectives → identify and assess quality risks → design and implement responses.

flashcards.front: When must an EQ review be complete?

flashcards.back: Annually if more than 100 issuer audit clients; at least every 3 years otherwise.
System: firms performing audits. Engagement: firms whose highest service is reviews or compilations.
